dna.fixture_why: The artifact stands as the whole ladder by default, which is what it is for. The SWEEP must see one rung at a time: capture_config_sweep unions the AABB across a spec's variants, so an all-rungs view in the same spec frames every single rung against a row several times its width and photographs it as a speck. That is not a hypothetical - it crashed the critic on a subject box too small to sample.
dna.framing_why: SOLVED, NOT GUESSED, by tools/solve_framing.py. At framing 1.0 this artifact's subject bounding box filled 25.9% of frame width and 40.0% of its height, with a subject share of 1.25%. The visible frame is 2 * PAD * radius * framing metres wide, so the box grows as 1/framing; solving for a target of 78% of the smaller-headroom dimension gives 0.33. THE ARTIFACT WAS NEVER DARK, EMPTY OR MISSING A FIXTURE - the camera was between three and eight times too far away, and the near-zero subject share this token had on record was a fact about the standpoint rather than about the axis.

predicted_degeneracy.arithmetic: Each level is 0.62 of the last, so level 5's segments are 0.62^4 = 0.148 of the trunk. They are numerous - 243 of them - but each is thin and short, so they add area without adding outline. NOTE THIS IS THE WAVE'S DIVERGENT LADDER and its closest pair should still be looser than octave_stack's. If depth's top pair comes in TIGHTER than octaves', the wave's central claim is refuted.
predicted_degeneracy.registered: 2026-08-15, BEFORE the first capture. RESTORED the same day after tools/apply_dna_block.py's lazy regex swallowed this key while re-deriving an empty axes object; text verbatim from the pre-registration.

depth_well.description: One recursion at depths one to five, the same small integer the octave family offers and the opposite curve: each level acts on everything the last one made, so the parts multiply where octaves halve. Same control, same word, no limit object.
